flags: Iridium agreed in a merger agreement to be acquired by Rocket Lab. Iridium stockholders have since approved the merger, and closing still depends on remaining regulatory approvals and other conditions.

Iridium closed its acquisition of Aireon Holdings, buying the remaining 60.5% of equity for an aggregate contractual purchase price of approximately $366.7 million, half in cash and half deferred as a seller loan. Iridium reported a $103.9 million gain related to the acquisition.

Iridium entered into a fourth amendment to its credit agreement. The amendment provides that the Rocket Lab transaction is not a change of control, and the term loans and revolving facility can remain outstanding after closing.
no_value_reason: implied borrowing cost outside the allowed range

pending_offer.claim: Iridium agreed in a merger agreement to be acquired by Rocket Lab. Iridium stockholders have since approved the merger, and closing still depends on remaining regulatory approvals and other conditions.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 business description.
business_model.claim: Iridium sells global voice, data and positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) satellite services over its low-Earth-orbit, L-band network, which has 66 operational satellites with in-orbit spares.
quotes: is a leading provider of global voice, data, and positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) satellite services

business_model.basis: Line items are from the Q3 income statement. The margin statement is from the 10-K MD&A.
business_model.claim: Revenue comes from three lines. In Q3 2026 service revenue was 187,498, subscriber equipment 19,045 and engineering and support services 39,190, for total revenue of 245,733 (table in thousands of dollars).
quotes: We recognize revenue primarily from the provision of services and the sale of equipment.
Voice and data, IoT data and broadband service revenues have historically generated higher margins than subscriber equipment revenue, and we expect this trend to continue.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A. The counter is stated in the 10-K MD&A uncertainties list.
business_model.claim: Commercial customers are reached mainly through a wholesale distribution network of about 130 service providers, 300 value-added resellers and 100 value-added manufacturers, which integrate Iridium services into their own products and applications.
quotes: We primarily sell our products and services to commercial end users by recruiting and expanding a global wholesale distribution network

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1, MD&A and risk factors.
business_model.claim: The U.S. government is the largest single customer, at $257.0 million or 29% of 2025 revenue. A large part of that comes from the EMSS contract, a fixed annual fee of $110.5 million that does not vary with subscribers or usage.
quotes: The service fee under the EMSS contract is fixed at $110.5 million per year for the remainder of the term and is not based on subscribers or usage, allowing an unlimited number of users access to these services.

business_model.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 earnings release.
business_model.claim: The Space Force exercised its option to extend the EMSS contract at the same contractual rate, and Iridium continues to expect a renewal in 2027.
quotes: Iridium continues to expect a renewal of the EMSS Contract in 2027.

business_model.claim: Commercial service is the largest part of the business, at 65% of Q3 2026 revenue. Commercial service revenue was $159.9 million, up 16% mainly because of the Aireon acquisition. Hosted payload and other data service rose $22.7 million, or 121%.
quotes: Commercial service remained the largest part of Iridium’s business, representing 65% of the Company’s total revenue during the third quarter.

business_model.basis: Figures are from the earnings release tables. The competition point is from the MD&A uncertainties.
business_model.claim: Subscriber volume and price both move commercial service revenue. Total billable subscribers reached 2,696,000, up 6%. IoT data revenue was 48,669 against 46,707 (table in thousands of dollars), up 4%, while IoT ARPU fell to $7.63 from $7.95.
quotes: Total billable subscribers grew 6% year-over-year, led by growth in commercial Internet of Things (IoT).

business_model.basis: Q3 figures are from the earnings release. The expectation was stated in the 10-K MD&A before the 2026 results.
business_model.claim: Equipment and engineering revenue were both lower in Q3 2026. Equipment was $19.0 million against $21.5 million, and engineering and support was $39.2 million against $40.2 million. Management expects engineering revenue to be higher in 2026 than in 2025.
quotes: We expect engineering and support service revenue to be higher in 2026 than in 2025.

business_model.basis: Figures are from the statements and release. The mechanism is partly inferred from the cost line descriptions.
business_model.claim: Costs combine a largely fixed network base with large changes in selling, general and administrative expense. In Q3 2026 SG&A was 74,936 against 35,508 and cost of services 60,666 against 50,762, while depreciation and amortization was 62,094 (all in thousands of dollars). Transaction-related expenses were 21,294.
quotes: which relies in part on our ability to leverage our largely fixed-cost infrastructure

business_model.basis: Stated in the statements and the OEBITDA reconciliation.
business_model.claim: Higher costs cut profit even as revenue grew. Q3 2026 operating income was 31,618 against 70,085, and operational EBITDA was 135,621 against 136,587 (all in thousands of dollars).

business_model.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement and the earnings release.
business_model.claim: The model is capital-intensive and debt-financed. Nine-month capital expenditures were 79,238 against operating cash flow of 281,706 (thousands of dollars), and gross debt was $2.2 billion with net leverage of 4.2 times trailing twelve-month operational EBITDA.
quotes: The Company ended the third quarter with net leverage of 4.2 times trailing twelve months OEBITDA.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the earnings release.
business_model.claim: A pending acquisition by Rocket Lab will change the ownership context. Each Iridium share is to receive $27.00 in cash plus Rocket Lab stock under a collar, and closing is expected by mid-2027.
quotes: The transaction is expected to be completed by mid-2027, subject to the satisfaction of the remaining regulatory approvals and closing conditions.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items (company self-description)
competitive_position.claim: Iridium describes its position as the only commercial provider with true global coverage. It runs a low-Earth-orbit, L-band constellation of 66 operational satellites with in-orbit spares, routed through crosslinks between satellites.
quotes: We are the only commercial provider of communications services offering true global coverage, connecting people, organizations and assets to and from anywhere, in real time.
which has an architecture of 66 operational satellites with in-orbit spares and related ground infrastructure

competitive_position.claim: The customer base is growing. Billable subscribers reached 2,696,000 at September 30, 2026, up 154,000, or 6%, from 2,542,000 a year earlier. Growth was led by commercial IoT.
quotes: Total billable subscribers grew 6% year-over-year, led by growth in commercial Internet of Things (IoT).

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items; the core-line split comes from the P6 revenue table
competitive_position.claim: Recent revenue growth comes mainly from the Aireon acquisition. Q3 total revenue was 8% higher year over year and service revenue rose 13%.
quotes: Service revenue grew 13% from the year-ago period, primarily due to the acquisition of Aireon, and was 76% of total revenue for the third quarter of 2026.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited tables; the link between SG&A and transaction costs is inferred from the OEBITDA reconciliation
competitive_position.claim: Profitability weakened in Q3 despite higher revenue. Operating income fell to 31,618 from 70,085 as SG&A rose to 74,936 from 35,508. Operational EBITDA was 135,621 against 136,587. Net income was lifted by a gain of 103,868 on equity method investments.
The U.S. government is the anchor customer, and the EMSS contract was extended to March 2027 at the same rate. Iridium expects a renewal in 2027.
quotes: The U.S. government, directly and indirectly, has been and continues to be our largest single customer, generating $257.0 million in revenue, representing 29% of our total revenue, for the year ended December 31, 2025.
On September 11, 2026, the U.S. Space Force exercised its option to extend the EMSS Contract with Iridium through March 2027, at the same contractual rate.

competitive_position.claim: Dependence on U.S. government contracts is a named threat. The government can terminate its agreements for convenience, and funding depends on budget decisions and shutdowns.
quotes: The U.S. government may terminate these agreements, in whole or in part, at any time for its convenience.

competitive_position.claim: Iridium closed its acquisition of Aireon on July 2, 2026, buying the remaining 60.5% for about $366.7 million. This extends its position into space-based air-traffic surveillance. Hosted payload and other data revenue rose $22.7 million, or 121%, in Q3.
quotes: acquiring the remaining 60.5% of equity interests in Aireon Holdings that we did not already own
Hosted payload and other data service revenue increased $22.7 million, or 121%, in the third quarter, primarily due to the acquisition of Aireon.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items; the effect on flexibility is inferred
competitive_position.claim: Financial flexibility is reduced after the Aireon deal. Net leverage was 4.2 times trailing OEBITDA, gross debt was $2.2 billion against cash of $97.9 million, and short-term secured debt rose to 214,346 from 3,402 at year-end 2025.
quotes: The Company ended the third quarter with net leverage of 4.2 times trailing twelve months OEBITDA.

competitive_position.claim: Iridium is positioning for direct-to-device and IoT use. Its L-band frequencies and technology were accepted into the 3GPP standard, so a planned service can be reached through standards-based cellular chipsets.
quotes: Iridium frequencies and technology were accepted as part of 3GPP Release 19, which allows Iridium NTN Direct to be accessible via cellular chipsets designed to 3GPP standards.

competitive_position.claim: The main competitive threat named is new satellite competition, especially SpaceX's plans for global direct-to-device service using acquired spectrum. Other threats are new LEO constellations and terrestrial expansion.
quotes: increased competition or potential competition from other satellite service providers, including SpaceX following its recently announced plans to acquire a significant amount of spectrum enabling global D2D services

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items; the dependence point is inferred from the risk list
competitive_position.claim: Iridium sells through a broad wholesale network of roughly 130 service providers, 300 value-added resellers and 100 value-added manufacturers. This is a channel advantage, and it also makes Iridium dependent on partners.

A pending acquisition by Rocket Lab shapes the company's outlook. Holders are to receive $27.00 in cash plus Rocket Lab shares, at a stated notional value of $54.00 per share, with closing expected by mid-2027. Interim covenants and a $223.6 million termination fee constrain Iridium until then.
quotes: The transaction has a notional value of $54.00 per share of Iridium common stock.

financial_health.basis: stated in the earnings release; the rise is read from the two printed net debt figures
financial_health.claim: Leverage rose with the Aireon deal. Gross debt was 2,159,458 and net debt 2,061,605 (table in thousands) against net debt of 1,736,188 a year earlier. Net leverage was 4.2 times trailing twelve months OEBITDA.
quotes: The Company ended the third quarter with net leverage of 4.2 times trailing twelve months OEBITDA.
The Company ended the third quarter with gross debt of $2.2 billion, and a cash and cash equivalents balance of $97.9 million, for a net debt balance of $2.1 billion.

financial_health.basis: balance sheet figures are stated; the link to the seller loan is inferred from the timing and size of the loan

financial_health.basis: stated in the cited items; the date of the seller loan is inferred from the July 2, 2026 closing date in P4

an aggregate principal balance of $154.7 million with a scheduled maturity date of October 10, 2028
